**Finding submitted — T4C: deviation (preferred-level cure).**

- **Issue:** §13.2 is Ono's only convenience exit, but it is unavailable until a redacted period after First Commercial Sale of *both* Products, in a term that runs until the Secondary Royalty Terms expire (§13.1). The notice period is redacted, so neither the preferred 30-day nor the fallback 60–90-day position can be verified, and there is no pro rata refund of prepaid amounts.
- **Array side is fine:** its termination rights are cause-based only (§§13.3, 13.4, 8.2) — not flagged, and our edit records the no-convenience position expressly.
- **Cure:** one surgical replace of §13.2 — delete the commencement gate, fix notice at thirty (30) days, add a pro rata refund of fees prepaid for post-termination periods, and confirm Array has no convenience right; the rationale-notice requirement and all other termination mechanics are preserved verbatim.
- **Noted, not flagged twice:** the §8.2 Competing Product tail and §6.1 non-refundable upfront fee are consequences, not early-termination fees; the refund language is scoped to post-termination periods to avoid conflict with §6.1.
